(def interleave
  "Returns a lazy seq of the first item in each coll, then the second etc."
  (fn
    ([] ())
    ([c1] (new LazySeq nil (fn* [] c1) nil nil))
    ([c1 c2]
     (new LazySeq nil (fn* []
      (let [s1 (seq c1) s2 (seq c2)]
        (when (and s1 s2)
          (cons (first s1) (cons (first s2)
                                 (interleave (rest s1) (rest s2))))))) nil nil))
    ([c1 c2 & colls]
     (new LazySeq nil (fn* []
      (let [ss (map seq (conj colls c2 c1))]
        (when (every? identity ss)
          (concat (map first ss) (apply interleave (map rest ss)))))) nil nil))))
rationale: Expand the complete pinned defn to def/fn, retaining its documentation (#30). lazy-seq is written as its expansion, a LazySeq of a thunk, since core is compiled before the macro. Clojure's interleave has the same arities and laziness.
